links.outcome: Readability (FDRE) of patient-friendly vs original reports, and share meeting quality and readability criteria
links.effect: Mean FDRE increase 54.2 ± 18.8 (p < 0.001); only 48.0% of combined main report and conclusion sections met both quality and readability criteria (FDRE > 60).
links.quote: Compared with original reports, patient-friendly reports were longer (median increase 65 words [48-84], p < 0.001) and had higher FDRE scores (mean increase 54.2 ± 18.8, p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Frequency of clinically relevant hallucinations in LLM patient-friendly report translations
links.effect: Clinically relevant hallucinations occurred in 45 reports (12.5%); 71.0% of main reports and 96.0% of conclusions met accuracy/completeness criteria.
links.quote: Clinically relevant hallucinations occurred in 45 reports (12.5%).

unlisted_practices: Locally hosted LLM to avoid cloud transfer of report text

screen.reason: Retrospective evaluation of a local LLM to translate radiology reports for patients, measuring quality, readability, and hallucinations, without testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard variation.
